title: Equivariant formal Cohen presentations with prime-to-ell invariant quotient
statement:
Let $A$ be a complete Noetherian normal local domain of dimension $d\geq2$, and let $\ell$ be a prime whose image in $A$ is a unit. There exist a complete Noetherian normal local domain $B$, a finite group $H$ acting on $B$ by local ring automorphisms, a coefficient subring $V\subseteq B$ preserved by $H$, an integer $r\geq1$, and an injective local ring map
$$R=V[[t_1,\ldots,t_r]]\longrightarrow B$$
which is finite as a module and $H$-equivariant, where $H$ fixes every $t_i$. There is an injective module-finite local map $A\to A^+=B^H$, the fixed subring, and $[\operatorname{Frac}(A^+):\operatorname{Frac}(A)]$ is prime to $\ell$. The order of $H$ is invertible in $V$. The map $V\to B$ induces an isomorphism on residue fields. In equal characteristic one can take $H=\{1\}$, $B=A^+=A$, $V$ a coefficient field and $r=d$. In mixed characteristic $(0,p)$ one can take $H$ an $\ell$-group, $V$ a complete discrete valuation ring of residue characteristic $p$, and $r=d-1$. In both cases there is $f\in R$ whose reduction modulo $\mathfrak m_V$ is nonzero, such that $R[1/f]\to B[1/f]$ is etale. Put $\Lambda=V^H$. This is a field in the field case and a complete discrete valuation ring in the discrete valuation case. The invariant formal ring is $R^H=\Lambda[[t_1,\ldots,t_r]]$. For every $0\leq j\leq r$, $\Lambda[[t_1,\ldots,t_j]]$ is complete regular Noetherian local of dimension $j$ in the field case and $j+1$ in the discrete valuation case, and $\ell$ is a unit in it.

Here a normal local domain is an integrally closed domain, a group action means a homomorphism into ring automorphisms, and the fixed subring consists of the elements fixed by every group element. Completeness and power series have the meanings of [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion], [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series]; Noetherianity, dimension, regularity, discrete valuation rings, finite modules, and etaleness are as in [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring], [def-weil-regular-scheme], [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring], [def-weil-finitely-generated-module], [def-weil-etale-morphism].

source.place: IV Theorem 2.1.1 (equal positive characteristic), IV Theorem 4.3.1 and 4.3.7 (mixed characteristic), pp.50 and 59--61; equal characteristic zero is the Cohen finite presentation and generic separability. Invariant coefficient DVR and power-series rings: IV 2.2.3, 4.3.5 and V 3.2.1--3.2.4. This is the formal presentation input, before any ideal is algebraized.

proof.text: First record the regularity calculation for any field or complete DVR $\Lambda$. For $S_j=\Lambda[[t_1,\ldots,t_j]]$, the cited power-series nodes give a Noetherian local domain, complete for its maximal ideal (apply completeness with coefficient ideal $0$ or $(\varpi)$). By the unit criterion and the quotient-by-variables statement, its maximal ideal is $(t_1,\ldots,t_j)$ over a field and $(t_1,\ldots,t_j,\varpi)$ over a DVR. The generator bound gives dimension at most $j$ or $j+1$. The chain $(0)\subsetneq(t_1)\subsetneq\cdots\subsetneq(t_1,\ldots,t_j)$, appending $(t_1,\ldots,t_j,\varpi)$ in the DVR case, gives the reverse inequality: each quotient before the last is a power-series domain, the last quotient is a field, and the next variable or uniformizer is nonzero in the preceding quotient. Thus the dimensions are $j$ and $j+1$, and these maximal-ideal generators prove regularity by its cited definition. This includes $j=0$.

source.place: V 3.1.3; regular power-series base, with the parameter-chain calculation expanded

proof.text: In equal characteristic $p>0$, apply the tame equivariant Cohen–Gabber node to $C=A$, $e=d$ and the trivial group. A domain is reduced and equidimensional. Take $V=s(k)$, $B=A^+=A$, $r=d$, and use its finite injective local parameter map. Its generic algebra is a finite product of finite separable fields. Apply the finite-algebra étale-neighbourhood node at the zero prime of $R=V[[T_1,\ldots,T_d]]$; $R$ is Noetherian by step 1, the local base is its fraction field, and torsion freeness and the generic-fibre hypothesis come from Cohen–Gabber. It gives $f\ne0$ with $R[1/f]\to A[1/f]$ étale. Reduction modulo $\mathfrak m_V=0$ is nonzero. The residue-field isomorphism is the section property. The quotient degree is $1$.

In equal characteristic zero use the complete-local-domain finite-over-regular node. Its coefficient ring is a field $V$: a Cohen DVR with prime uniformizer cannot map locally into a ring of residue characteristic zero. It gives a finite injective local map $R=V[[T_1,\ldots,T_r]]\to A$ with residue isomorphism. Finiteness implies integrality, and integral injective maps preserve dimension; step 1 therefore gives $r=d$. Set $B=A^+=A$ and $H=\{1\}$. The fraction-degree node gives a finite field extension $\operatorname{Frac}(A)/\operatorname{Frac}(R)$, separable by the characteristic-zero node. Moreover $A\otimes_R\operatorname{Frac}(R)=\operatorname{Frac}(A)$: the localized domain is finite-dimensional over the base field, so multiplication by a nonzero element is an injective and hence bijective linear map. Apply the finite-algebra étale-neighbourhood node at $(0)$, alternative (ii), to obtain $f\ne0$. Again reduction modulo the coefficient maximal ideal is unchanged.

source.place: Equal characteristic zero: Stacks 032D (lemma-complete-local-Noetherian-domain-finite-over-regular), 00GK, 00OK and generic separability

proof.text: Suppose now $A$ has mixed characteristic $(0,p)$. Since $\ell$ is a unit, $\ell\ne p$. Apply the Galois Epp preparation node to obtain $A\hookrightarrow B$, $W\hookrightarrow B$, a group $G$, a uniformizer $\pi$ of $W$, and $D=B/\pi B$ reduced equidimensional of dimension $e=d-1\geq1$, with perfect subfield $k_0=W/\pi W$. The residue field is $k'=B/\mathfrak n_B$, and $\dim B=d$. Choose an $\ell$-Sylow subgroup $H\leq G$ by the cited Sylow node. Its order is a power of $\ell$, hence invertible in $W$, in $B$ and in $k'$. Restrict the compatible actions to $H$. The ideal $\pi B$ is stable even if $\pi$ itself is not fixed, because every local automorphism of $W$ preserves its maximal ideal.

source.place: IV 4.3.3–4.3.5, Galois Epp base change and choice of an ℓ-Sylow

proof.text: Apply tame equivariant Cohen–Gabber to $D$ with its $H$-action. It gives an equivariant section $s:k'\to D$, respecting $k_0$, and fixed parameters $u_1,\ldots,u_e$ with finite injective generically separable map $k'[[T_1,\ldots,T_e]]\to D$. Apply the equivariant Cohen coefficient-lift node to $(W,B,H,s)$: completeness and Noetherianity are supplied by step 4, the order is a unit in $W$, and $s$ is precisely the required equivariant $k_0$-section. Obtain $V$ with residue field $k'$, uniformizer $\pi$, and an equivariant local map $\psi:V\to B$ lifting $s$. It is injective: every nonzero element of $V$ is a unit times a power of $\pi$ by the cited DVR node, while the image of $\pi$ is nonzero in the domain $B$. For each $u_i$ choose a lift $b_i\in\mathfrak n_B$ and replace it by $x_i=|H|^{-1}\sum_{h\in H}h(b_i)$. This is $H$-fixed, lies in $\mathfrak n_B$, and reduces to $u_i$.

source.place: IV 4.3.5–4.3.6: equivariant special-fibre parameters, coefficient lift and averaged variable lifts

proof.text: Evaluate formal series using $\psi$ and the $x_i$ by the power-series universal-property node, giving $\varphi:R=V[[T_1,\ldots,T_e]]\to B$. The evaluation formula shows equivariance term by term, since $\psi$ is equivariant and the $x_i$ are fixed. Its reduction modulo $\pi$ is the Cohen–Gabber map of step 5: coefficientwise reduction identifies $R/\pi R$ with $k'[[T]]$ (lift each coefficient; the kernel consists exactly of series divisible by $\pi$). Since $\sqrt{(u_1,\ldots,u_e)D}=\mathfrak n_D$, we have $\sqrt{(\pi,x_1,\ldots,x_e)B}=\mathfrak n_B$. Apply case (b) of the formal-normalization node, with $\dim B=e+1$, to conclude that $\varphi$ is injective, local, module-finite, torsion free and a residue-field isomorphism. Thus $r=e=d-1$.

source.place: IV 4.3.7 and 4.2.5: lift the parameter map and check formal normalization

proof.text: The prime $\mathfrak p=\pi R$ has domain quotient $k'[[T_1,\ldots,T_e]]$ by the domain node and the coefficient reduction of step 6. Multiplication by $\pi$ in $R$ is injective coefficientwise. The principal-prime localization node therefore gives that $R_{\mathfrak p}$ is a DVR. Its residue field is $K=\operatorname{Frac}(k'[[T]])$. The fibre $B\otimes_R\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ is $D\otimes_{k'[[T]]}K$, identified by the quotient and localization presentations, and is a finite product of finite separable extensions of $K$ by step 5. Use alternative (ii) of the finite-algebra étale-neighbourhood node; the base is Noetherian by step 1 and finiteness and torsion freeness are supplied by step 6. It gives $f\notin\pi R$ with $R[1/f]\to B[1/f]$ étale. Its reduction modulo $\mathfrak m_V=(\pi)$ is exactly nonzero, as required.

source.place: IV 4.3.7: étaleness over a p-dense base open

proof.text: Put $A^+=B^H$. It contains $A$. As an $A$-submodule of the finite module $B$, it is finite by the Noetherian submodule node. An element of $B^H$ is a unit there exactly when it is a unit in $B$, because its inverse is again fixed. Thus $B^H$ is local with maximal ideal $\mathfrak n_B\cap B^H$, and $A\to B^H$ is local and injective. For normality, if $z\in\operatorname{Frac}(B^H)$ is integral over $B^H$, its same monic equation makes it integral over $B$; normality of $B$ gives $z\in B$, and writing $z$ as a quotient of fixed elements makes it fixed. Also $\operatorname{Frac}(B^H)=\operatorname{Frac}(B)^H$: for fixed $a/b$, multiply numerator and denominator by $\prod_{h\ne1}h(b)$ to make the denominator $\prod_hh(b)$ fixed; the resulting numerator is then fixed too. By Galois Epp, $L=\operatorname{Frac}(B)$ is finite Galois over $K=\operatorname{Frac}(A)$ with full group $G$. The finite-Galois fixed-field node gives $L^G=K$ and $[L:K]=|G|$; the fixed-degree node applied to the faithful subgroup $H$ gives $[L:L^H]=|H|$. Degree multiplicativity gives $[L^H:K]=[G:H]$, prime to $\ell$ by step 4. This proves the quotient clause.

source.place: IV 4.3.7 and V 3.2.3(i): invariant quotient and generic prime-to-ℓ degree

proof.text: It remains to describe $\Lambda=V^H$ in mixed characteristic. Use the DVR unit-times-uniformizer-power node to write $v$ for the exponent valuation on $\operatorname{Frac}(V)$. Local automorphisms preserve $v$. Fixed nonzero fractions are quotients of fixed elements by the norm-denominator calculation of step 8, so $F=\operatorname{Frac}(V)^H=\operatorname{Frac}(\Lambda)$, and $\Lambda=\{z\in F:v(z)\geq0\}$. The nonzero element $\prod_hh(\pi)\in\Lambda$ has positive valuation; let $a\in\Lambda$ have the least positive valuation $q$. For any nonzero element of $F$, divide its valuation by $q$; after dividing by a power of $a$, a positive remainder would give an element of $\Lambda$ of valuation strictly between $0$ and $q$. Thus $v(F^\times)=q\mathbf Z$, and every nonzero ideal of $\Lambda$ is generated by an element of least valuation. It is a nonfield local PID, hence a DVR by the cited definition. Finally $\Lambda\cap\pi^nV=a^{\lceil n/q\rceil}\Lambda$. A compatible system modulo powers of $a$ is therefore Cauchy in $V$ and converges there by completeness. Its limit is fixed, since every $h$ preserves all powers of $\pi$, and lies in $\Lambda$. Separation follows from separation of $V$. This proves that $\Lambda$ is a complete DVR.

source.place: Invariant coefficient calculation from IV 2.2.3, expanded directly by valuations and completeness

proof.text: In equal characteristic $H$ is trivial, so $\Lambda=V$ is the coefficient field. In either case the action on $R$ is coefficientwise with every variable fixed, and equality of series is equality of coefficients; hence $R^H=\Lambda[[t_1,\ldots,t_r]]$. The prime $\ell$ is a unit in $V$: in equal characteristic it is nonzero in the coefficient field, while in mixed characteristic $p\ne\ell$ and $V$ has residue characteristic $p$. Its inverse is fixed, so $\ell$ is a unit in $\Lambda$ and in each of its power-series rings. Apply step 1 to $\Lambda$ for every $0\leq j\leq r$ to obtain the final completeness, regularity, Noetherianity and dimension clauses. Both values of $r$ are positive since $d\geq2$.

source.place: V 3.2.1–3.2.4: fixed formal ring; coefficient and variable checks

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q99-adea5a2ff (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item, all 3 new nodes, every cited statement and the source places: ILO IV 2.2.2–2.2.6, 4.1.7–4.1.9, 4.2.3–4.2.5, 4.3.1–4.3.7, V 3.2.1–3.2.3. New nodes. (1) The tame equivariant Cohen–Gabber node is IV 2.2.2 restricted to equidimensional rings. The extra clauses (injective, torsion free, √(u) = 𝔫, generic algebra separable) follow from equidimensionality and reducedness. The perfect-subfield clause holds because every coefficient field contains each perfect subfield (p^n-th root argument plus Krull intersection). (2) The Galois Epp node is IV 4.3.3–4.3.5: Frac(W₀^ν) is algebraically closed in Frac(A), so Frac(C)/Frac(A) is Galois with the full group G. The special fibre is reduced by Epp and IV 4.2.4, and equidimensional because complete domains are catenary. (3) The equivariant coefficient-lift node is IV 4.3.5–4.3.6: the Galois action lifts to I(k′), and isobarycentres of lifts exist because |H| is invertible mod p. All three were tested on small cases, including Saito's IV 4.3.2 example and trivial or non-faithful H. None duplicates an existing node: lem-per-mixed-reduced-special-fibre-cover, lem-per-perfect-residue-coefficient-dvr and lem-per-cohen-gabber-finite-presentations are non-equivariant special cases, noted as overlaps. None restates an item clause. Steps 1–10: every hypothesis checks against the cited statements. Specifically: char-p and char-0 cases via the étale-neighbourhood node at (0); case (b) of parameter-ideal normalization with dim B = e+1; the principal-prime DVR node at πR; the degree [G:H] via the Galois fixed-field, fixed-degree and multiplicativity nodes; Λ = V^H a complete DVR via valuations, including H acting trivially on V; ℓ ∈ Λ^×. All clauses and all three characteristic cases are covered. There is no cycle and no Lean declaration states the item or a new node. Batch 5: lem-trf-finite-domain-fraction-degree and lem-trf-noetherian-submodule-finitely-presented are generic Mathlib leaves (finite fraction-field degree; Stacks 00FP). The parameter-ideal node's 47-node closure reaches only the first of them. Neither is part of the trace formula or Poincaré duality, so all three citations are accepted.
